mainTopic: Libation wine after pouring (burning, מעילה, plugging the שיתין), an אגדה on modesty, צדקה and חסד, and why the שבת water barrel was not consecrated
overview: This amud opens at the end of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's teaching that leftover libation wine is burned in holiness. רבינא learns this through a גזירה שוה on the word קדש. The גמרא then asks whose view fits the משנה that libations are subject to מעילה only until they reach the שיתין. Two versions of that discussion each end by showing it fits both opinions, since once an item's מצוה is done there is no מעילה. ריש לקיש teaches that the שיתין were plugged during wine libations, and רב פפא and רבא draw lessons about drinking wine from the word שכר. A long אגדה follows: פסוקים from שיר השירים about going up לרגל and learning Torah privately, then רבי אלעזר's teachings on modesty, צדקה and גמילות חסדים, along with a ברייתא and teachings on חן and 'תורת חסד.' Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה about water for שבת, and זעירי explains why the golden barrel was not consecrated. That explanation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Libation wine is burned in holiness, just as it is poured in holiness
steps.stepSummary: This line ends רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's statement: just as נסכים are poured in קדושה, their leftovers must be burned in קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as its pouring is done in holiness, so too its burning must be done in holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's teaching (begun on the previous amud) that leftover libation wine was collected and burned in a holy manner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק holds that the wine did not drain away into the depths. It collected near the מזבח and was later burned. He compares the end of the wine to its beginning: it started in קדושה, so it must also end in קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness; a sanctified manner or place

phrases.english: Just as its pouring is in holiness,
so too its burning is in holiness.
phrases.notes: End of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק's statement, which began on the previous amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּיסּוּכוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה, כָּךְ שְׂרֵיפָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover libation wine must be burned in קדושה, just as it was poured in קדושה.

steps.title: Where does the verse show that burning is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק about pouring in holiness tells us anything about burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. The פסוק only talks about pouring, so where does burning come from? This sets up רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'בקדש הסך נסך' clearly speaks about pouring, not burning. The גמרא wants to know what textual link lets us add a requirement of burning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? (a request for the textual source)

phrases.english: From where is it implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the burning law stated in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source shows that the leftover wine must be burned?

steps.title: רבינא learns burning through the shared word 'holy'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers with a גזירה שוה: the word קדש appears for libations and also for leftover קרבנות, which must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is learned from 'holy' and 'holy.' Here it is written: 'In holiness shall you pour a libation,' and there it is written: 'You shall burn the leftover in fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא shows that the word קדש links libations to leftover sacrificial meat, so libation wine must also be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מילואים says leftover holy food must be burned because it is 'קדש.' Since libations are also called 'קדש,' the גזירה שוה applies the same burning rule to leftover libation wine.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes / is learned (introduces a גזירה שוה)
It is written here... and it is written there (the two sides of a comparison)
Leftover holy food that must be burned
A derivation based on the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is derived from 'holy' and 'holy.'
It is written here: 'In holiness shall you pour a libation,'
and it is written there: 'And you shall burn the leftover in fire;'
it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word קדש links libations to נותר, which must be burned.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, leftover libation wine must be burned, and רבינא learns this through the קדש–קדש גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Whose view is the teaching about misusing libations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching: libations are subject to מעילה at first, but once they go down the שיתין they no longer are. Whose opinion is this?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this teaching follow? 'Libations: at first, one can commit misuse with them. Once they went down to the drainpipes, one cannot commit misuse with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and quotes a teaching about מעילה with libations. It is setting up an attempt to match this teaching to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק or to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching implies that after the wine reaches the שיתין, it is still physically present and the question of מעילה is relevant, but it does not apply. The גמרא wants to see which side of the earlier מחלוקת about where the wine ends up fits this best.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom does it go?
Drainpipes / pits under the מזבח where libations flowed

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which is taught:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, דְּתַנְיָא. The source quoted here is really a משנה in מעילה.

phrases.english: Libations: at first, one commits misuse with them.
Once they went down to the drainpipes, one does not commit misuse with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the source for burning to which opinion matches a teaching about מעילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the מעילה teaching follow רבי אלעזר בר צדוק or the רבנן?

steps.title: Suggestion that it follows רבי אלעזר בר צדוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the teaching follows רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, because according to the רבנן the wine would already be gone into the depths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is רבי אלעזר בר צדוק. For if it were the רבנן, the wine has already gone down to the depths!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tentatively proposes that the teaching matches רבי אלעזר בר צדוק and gives a reason for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the wine flows down into the תהום, so it is out of reach and there is nothing to discuss. Only according to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, who says the wine stays and collects, does it make sense to say that מעילה does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The deep / abyss beneath the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק הִיא,
phrases.english: Let us say it is Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי רַבָּנַן, הָא נָחֲתוּ לְהוּ לִתְהוֹם!
phrases.english: for if it were the Rabbis, they have gone down to the depths!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to step 4's question.
steps.raayaObject: That the מעילה teaching follows רבי אלעזר בר צדוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: According to the רבנן the wine disappears into the תהום, so a ruling about its מעילה would have no subject.

steps.title: It can even follow the רבנן, when wine collected outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: the teaching can follow the רבנן too, in a case where some wine collected outside the drainpipes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it is the רבנן, it speaks of wine that was collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and shows the teaching works even for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the רבנן agree that some wine can miss the drainpipes and gather between the כבש and the מזבח. The teaching is talking about that wine, so it does not prove anything about רבי אלעזר בר צדוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (opens a rejection)
Was collected / absorbed (wine gathered outside the pipes)

phrases.english: Even if you say it is the Rabbis,
it refers to wine that was collected.
phrases.notes: Wine that splashed outside the drainpipes and pooled between the ramp and the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's proposed attribution.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that only רבי אלעזר בר צדוק can fit the teaching.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed all wine reaches the תהום for the רבנן, but wine that collected outside the pipes is still present.

steps.title: Second version: suggestion that it follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: A second version suggests the opposite: the teaching follows the רבנן, because according to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק the wine would still be holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Let us say it is the רבנן and not רבי אלעזר בר צדוק? For if it were רבי אלעזר, the wine still remains in its holiness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second version of the discussion that reaches the opposite tentative conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, the collected wine must still be burned in קדושה, so it seems to be still holy. If so, מעילה should apply, which contradicts the teaching that says it does not. So this version suggests the teaching fits only the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against step 6. It is a different version of the same discussion, from another tradition of how the exchange went.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבָּנַן הִיא, וְלָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק?
phrases.english: Let us say it is the Rabbis, and not Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אַכַּתִּי בִּקְדוּשְׁתַּיְיהוּ קָיְימִי!
phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Elazar, they still remain in their holiness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the attribution question from step 4 in a different version.
steps.raayaObject: That the מעילה teaching follows the רבנן, not רבי אלעזר בר צדוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: According to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק the wine must be burned in קדושה, so it seems still holy and subject to מעילה.

steps.title: Once a מצוה is done, misuse no longer applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion: even according to רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, once the מצוה has been done there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it is רבי אלעזר, there is nothing whose מצוה has been done and yet one commits misuse with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and shows the teaching can also fit רבי אלעזר בר צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine that must still be burned keeps a holy status. But מעילה stops once the item's מצוה, the pouring, is complete. So a requirement to burn does not mean מעילה still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no item (a general rule)
Whose מצוה has already been performed

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the teaching ends up fitting both opinions. The key general rule is: once an item's מצוה is done, there is no מעילה, even if it must still be disposed of in קדושה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין לך דבר שנעשה מצותו ומועלין בו' is a general principle of מעילה that appears in other places as well. It separates two things: a holy status that requires burning, and the law of מעילה.

phrases.english: Even if you say it is Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מִצְוָתוֹ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: there is nothing whose מצוה has been done and one commits misuse with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מִצְוָתוֹ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 7's proposed attribution.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי אלעזר בר צדוק cannot fit the teaching.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed that wine needing burning in קדושה must also be subject to מעילה. In fact, מעילה ends once the מצוה is done.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The teaching fits both opinions. A completed מצוה removes מעילה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the drainpipes were plugged during wine libations
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that when wine was poured on the מזבח, the שיתין were plugged, to fulfill 'בקדש הסך נסך שכר לה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: When they pour wine on top of the altar, they plug the drainpipes, to fulfill what is said: 'In holiness shall you pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from ריש לקיש about how the wine libation was actually done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drainpipes were blocked so the wine would not run straight down into the תהום. Instead it filled up the שיתין beneath the מזבח, so the libation stayed 'בקדש,' in the holy place. The word שכר suggests a full, satisfying pouring, and the next steps explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: Strong drink; a full, satisfying drink

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמְּנַסְּכִין יַיִן עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: When they pour wine on top of the altar,
they plug the drainpipes,
to fulfill what is stated:
'In holiness shall you pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמְּנַסְּכִין יַיִן עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new teaching about how the wine libation was performed, using the same פסוק from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During wine libations the שיתין are plugged, to fulfill 'בקדש הסך נסך שכר לה׳.'

steps.title: Where Does the Verse Show the Pipes Were Plugged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק 'בקדש הסך נסך שכר לה׳' shows that the שיתין were plugged.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we see this from the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how ריש לקיש's verse proves that the שיתין were plugged. It is setting up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse does not say anything clear about plugging pipes. The גמרא wants to know which word in it points to this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this implied? Where do we see it?
The drainpipes under the מזבח where the wine flowed down

phrases.english: From where is it implied?
phrases.notes: Asks how ריש לקיש's verse shows that the pipes were plugged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of ריש לקיש's statement in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of 'בקדש הסך נסך שכר לה׳' shows that the שיתין were plugged.

steps.title: The Word שכר Means Drinking, Fullness, and Intoxication
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that שכר means drinking, filling up, and intoxication. That requires the wine to collect and fill up, so the pipes had to be plugged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: 'שכר' is a word for drinking, a word for being full, and a word for being drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the word שכר holds three ideas: drinking, filling up, and getting drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'full' and 'drunk' means more than a small amount. The wine had to fill up the area by the מזבח, and that only happens if the pipes are plugged.

keyTerms.meaning: Intoxicating drink; here it hints at drinking, fullness, and intoxication
An expression of, a word that means

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
'Shechar' is an expression of drinking,
an expression of fullness, an expression of intoxication.
phrases.notes: Fullness means the wine filled up the space, so the pipes had to be plugged.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שֵׁכָר לְשׁוֹן שְׁתִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word שכר implies fullness, which needs the wine to collect, so the שיתין were plugged.

steps.title: Wine Satisfies From the Throat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from this that a person feels full from wine when it fills his throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that when a person gets full from wine, he gets full from his throat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a side lesson about how wine makes a person feel satisfied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the 'fullness' of the נסך came from the wine filling up the space, a person feels satisfied from wine when it fills his throat. With food it is different, because food satisfies when it fills the stomach.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this
that when a person is satisfied from wine,
he is satisfied from his throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical inference from the explanation of שכר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person feels satisfied from wine when it fills his throat.

steps.title: Advice for a Scholar With Little Wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא advises a young scholar who does not have much wine to drink it in big gulps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A young Torah scholar who does not have much wine should drink it in big gulps.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives practical advice based on רב פפא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine satisfies by filling the throat. So someone with only a little wine gets the most enjoyment by taking big gulps that fill his throat.

keyTerms.meaning: He should swallow in big gulps

phrases.english: Rava said: A young Torah scholar
who does not have much wine
should swallow it in big gulps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב פפא's point in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar with little wine should drink in big gulps to feel the most satisfied.

steps.title: רבא's Own Practice With the Cup of Blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבא himself drank the כוס של ברכה in big gulps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would drink the כוס של ברכה in big gulps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what רבא himself did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used his own advice for a מצוה cup. He drank the wine of the מצוה in the most satisfying way.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of blessing, the cup over which ברכת המזון or another blessing is said

phrases.english: Rava, with the cup of blessing,
would swallow it in big gulps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבא's own practice, which matches his advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא drank the כוס של ברכה in big gulps.

steps.title: The Beautiful Steps of the Jewish People Going Up for the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains 'מה יפו פעמיך בנעלים בת נדיב' as praise for the Jewish people going up לרגל. He says בת נדיב means the daughter of אברהם אבינו, who is called נדיב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the verse 'How beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of the noble one' mean? How beautiful are the steps of the Jewish people when they go up לרגל. 'Daughter of the noble one' means the daughter of אברהם אבינו, who is called noble, as it says: 'The nobles of the nations gathered, the people of the God of אברהם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to more teachings on פסוקים in שיר השירים. רבא explains a verse about the Jewish people going up to ירושלים for the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Steps' means the people's footsteps going up לרגל. 'בת נדיב' is the Jewish people, the daughter of אברהם, because תהלים calls אברהם's followers 'נדיבי עמים'.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught or explained a verse
Going up to ירושלים for the festival

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is meant by what is written:
'How beautiful are your steps in sandals, O daughter of the noble one'?
How beautiful are the steps of the Jewish people
at the time they go up for the festival.
'Daughter of the noble one': the daughter of Abraham our forefather,
who was called noble, as it is stated:
'The nobles of the nations gathered, the people of the God of Abraham.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic teaching from שיר השירים, linked to the earlier verses about the שיתין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בת נדיב' refers to the Jewish people, daughters of אברהם, whose steps going up לרגל are beautiful.

steps.title: Why Only the God of אברהם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the verse mentions only אברהם and not יצחק and יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The God of אברהם' — and not the God of יצחק and יעקב?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the verse in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jewish people come from all three אבות. So it seems strange for the verse to name only אברהם.

phrases.english: 'The God of Abraham' — and not the God of Isaac and Jacob?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם, וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the verse quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All three אבות are the ancestors of the Jewish people, so why is only אברהם mentioned?

steps.title: אברהם Was the First of the Converts
steps.stepSummary: Only אברהם is named because he was the first of the גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'the God of אברהם' is said because he was the first of the גרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אברהם is singled out because he was the very first convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks about 'nobles of the nations' gathering. That fits אברהם, who came from the nations and was the first to come close to ה׳.

phrases.english: Rather: 'the God of Abraham,'
who was the first of the converts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִילָּה לְגֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the purpose of the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only אברהם is mentioned, even though all three אבות are ancestors.
steps.terutzMaskana: אברהם is named as the first convert, which fits nations gathering to ה׳.

steps.title: Torah Is Like a Thigh: Best Kept Private
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב ענן learns from 'חמוקי ירכיך' that, just as a thigh is covered, Torah is best learned in private.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רב ענן: What is meant by 'The hidden parts of your thighs'? Why are words of Torah compared to a thigh? To tell you: just as a thigh is hidden, so too words of Torah should be in private.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching on the next phrase in the same verse of שיר השירים, about learning Torah privately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thigh is always covered by clothing. So the verse teaches that Torah study is at its best when done quietly, not as a public show.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study hall of
The hidden parts (curves) of your thighs

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַב עָנָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rav Anan: What is meant by what is written:
'The hidden parts of your thighs'?
Why are words of Torah compared to a thigh?
To tell you: just as a thigh is hidden,
so too words of Torah are in private.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַב עָנָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another aggadic explanation of the same verse in שיר השירים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah study is best done privately, like a thigh that is covered.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר on Walking Modestly With ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the teaching to רבי אלעזר's explanation of מיכה. 'והצנע לכת' refers to burying the dead and bringing a bride to the חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אלעזר said: What is meant by 'He told you, man, what is good, and what ה׳ asks of you: only to do justice, love kindness, and walk modestly with your God'? 'To do justice' is דין. 'Love kindness' is גמילות חסדים. 'Walk modestly with your God' is taking out the dead for burial and bringing a bride to the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the idea of keeping things private matches רבי אלעזר's teaching. It then quotes his explanation of the פסוק in מיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר links each part of the verse to a מצוה. 'Walking modestly' is linked to funerals and weddings, which must be done with modesty. This sets up the קל וחומר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what [so-and-so] said; this matches
Taking out the dead for burial
Bringing a bride to her wedding

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, מַאי דִּכְתִיב:
phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by what is written:
'He has told you, O man, what is good,
and what ה׳ requires of you:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם עֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט וְאַהֲבַת חֶסֶד
phrases.english: only to do justice and to love kindness
and to walk modestly with your God'?
'To do justice' — this is judgment;
'and to love kindness' — this is acts of kindness;
'and to walk modestly with your God' —

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הוֹצָאַת הַמֵּת וְהַכְנָסַת כַּלָּה לַחוּפָּה.
phrases.english: this is taking out the dead and bringing a bride to the wedding canopy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea of privacy from step 18 with רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that Torah and מצוות are best done privately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's reading of מיכה ו:ח, 'והצנע לכת'.

steps.title: A קל וחומר for Private מצוות
steps.stepSummary: If public מצוות like funerals and weddings must be done modestly, then private מצוות surely must be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is this not a קל וחומר? If for things that are usually done in public, the Torah says 'walk modestly,' then for things that are usually done in private, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אלעזר's teaching with a קל וחומר about doing מצוות privately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Funerals and weddings are normally public events, and still the Torah asks for modesty. Then מצוות that are naturally private, like צדקה and Torah learning, should certainly be kept private.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

steps.whatToRemember: Even public מצוות call for modesty. So מצוות that are naturally private, like צדקה and Torah learning, must certainly be done quietly. This backs up דבי רב ענן's lesson that Torah is like a hidden thigh.

phrases.english: And is this not a kal vachomer?
If for things that are normally done in public,
the Torah said 'walk modestly,'
then things that are normally done in private
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final קל וחומר from רבי אלעזר's reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מצוות that are naturally private, like Torah study and צדקה, must certainly be done modestly and privately.

steps.title: Charity is greater than all offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that doing צדקה is greater than bringing all the קרבנות, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A person who gives צדקה is greater than one who brings all the קרבנות, because the פסוק says: 'Doing צדקה and justice is more chosen by ה׳ than a מזבח offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new set of teachings from רבי אלעזר about the value of צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says צדקה is 'more chosen than a זבח.' It does not name any specific קרבן. So רבי אלעזר reads it as covering all קרבנות together.

keyTerms.meaning: Charity, giving money to the poor
Offerings brought in the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a whole chain of teachings that rank different kinds of good deeds against each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Greater is one who performs charity
than all the offerings,
as it is stated: “To perform charity and justice
is more acceptable to the Lord than an offering.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גָּדוֹל הָעוֹשֶׂה צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה section on צדקה. It follows the theme of מצוות like burial and weddings from the previous steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing צדקה is greater than offering all the קרבנות.

steps.title: Acts of kindness are greater than charity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה, because the פסוק says: 'Sow for yourselves with צדקה, and reap according to חסד.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר goes one level higher: if צדקה beats קרבנות, then גמילות חסדים beats צדקה. The next step will explain how the פסוק proves this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares צדקה to sowing and חסד to reaping. Here the proof is only quoted. The explanation of why reaping is 'better' comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts of kindness, personally helping others

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up צדקה with גמילות חסדים. צדקה here means giving money to the poor. גמילות חסדים is a wider idea of doing kindness.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Acts of kindness are greater
than charity,
as it is stated: “Sow to yourselves according to charity,
and reap according to kindness.”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גְּדוֹלָה גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a ladder on top of step 21: קרבנות, then צדקה above them, then גמילות חסדים above that.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה.

steps.title: Sowing is uncertain, reaping is certain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק: sowing does not guarantee you will eat, but reaping does. So חסד, which is compared to reaping, is greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person plants, maybe he will eat and maybe he won't. If a person harvests, he will surely eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק in step 22 proves that חסד is greater than צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting a seed is only a beginning. Many things can go wrong before it becomes food. Harvesting is the stage where the food is already in hand. Since צדקה is linked to sowing and חסד to reaping, חסד has the surer, fuller value.

phrases.english: If a person sows —
it is uncertain whether he will eat or not eat;
if a person reaps — he certainly eats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the proof-text quoted in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The sowing and reaping metaphor in הושע י:יב.

steps.title: Charity is rewarded by the kindness inside it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that the reward for צדקה depends on the חסד inside it, meaning the care and effort, using the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: צדקה is rewarded only according to the kindness that is in it, because the פסוק says: 'Sow with צדקה, and reap according to חסד.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same פסוק to teach a new idea: how the reward for צדקה is measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the פסוק compared צדקה and חסד as two separate things. Now רבי אלעזר reads it differently: you 'reap' your צדקה according to the חסד in it. The reward is not about the amount of money alone. It is about how kindly and thoughtfully the צדקה was given.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק as step 22, but it teaches a different point. Step 22 compared חסד to צדקה. This step talks about the חסד inside צדקה itself.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Charity is not rewarded
except according to the kindness within it,
as it is stated: “Sow to yourselves according to charity,
and reap according to kindness.”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין צְדָקָה מִשְׁתַּלֶּמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reuses the פסוק from step 22 for a new teaching about reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward for צדקה is measured by the kindness and care in it.

steps.title: Three ways kindness is greater than charity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three ways גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה: how it is done, who receives it, and whether it can help the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In three ways גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה. צדקה is done only with money, but חסד can be done with your body or your money. צדקה is only for the poor, but חסד is for poor and rich. צדקה is only for the living, but חסד is for the living and the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out exactly why גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר proved from a פסוק that חסד is greater. This ברייתא gives three concrete reasons. In each one, חסד reaches more: it can be done in more ways, it helps more kinds of people, and it even helps the dead, such as by burying them.
steps.whatToRemember: גמילות חסדים is wider than צדקה in three ways: body and money, poor and rich, living and dead.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
In three respects

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹלָה גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים יוֹתֵר מִן הַצְּדָקָה.
phrases.english: acts of kindness are greater than charity.
Charity — with one's money;

phrases.aramaic: גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים — בֵּין בְּגוּפוֹ, בֵּין בְּמָמוֹנוֹ.
phrases.english: acts of kindness — both with his person and with his money.
Charity — to the poor;

phrases.aramaic: גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים — בֵּין לָעֲנִיִּים בֵּין לָעֲשִׁירִים.
phrases.english: acts of kindness — both to the poor and to the rich.
Charity — to the living;

phrases.aramaic: גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים — בֵּין לַחַיִּים בֵּין לַמֵּתִים.
phrases.english: acts of kindness — both to the living and to the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and details רבי אלעזר's claim from step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גמילות חסדים is greater than צדקה in three ways: method, recipients, and reaching the dead.

steps.title: Doing charity and justice fills the world with kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that whoever does צדקה ומשפט is considered as if he filled the whole world with חסד, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Anyone who does צדקה and justice is considered as if he filled the entire world with kindness, because the פסוק says: 'He loves צדקה and justice; the earth is full of ה׳'s kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives another teaching about how great צדקה is. The next steps will ask follow-up questions about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'loves צדקה and justice' right next to 'the earth is full of חסד.' רבי אלעזר reads the two halves as connected. When a person does צדקה ומשפט, the world becomes full of חסד.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who performs charity and justice,

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ מִילֵּא כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ חֶסֶד.
phrases.english: it is as though he filled the whole world in its entirety with kindness.
As it is stated: “He loves charity and justice;
the earth is full of the kindness of the Lord.”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי אלעזר in the same series on צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who does צדקה ומשפט is considered to have filled the world with חסד.

steps.title: Can anyone who wants to do kindness simply do it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible mistake: since the reward is so great, maybe anyone who jumps to do חסד easily succeeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you will say: anyone who comes to jump in and do this can just jump in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a 'you might think' idea. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק will correct it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After hearing how huge the reward is, someone might assume doing real חסד is easy and open to everyone at any moment. The גמרא voices this assumption so it can push back on it.

phrases.english: Lest you say
that anyone who comes to leap may leap,

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר כׇּל הַבָּא לִקְפּוֹץ קוֹפֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible wrong conclusion someone might draw from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the great reward of חסד is easy for anyone to get.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reward is so great and freely available, maybe anyone can grab it at will.

steps.title: Real kindness is precious and rare
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'How precious is Your kindness' shows that doing חסד properly is rare and valuable. Not everyone easily gets to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'How precious is Your kindness, O God.' Doing kindness properly is precious and rare.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the mistaken idea from step 27 with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יקר' means precious, and also rare. Something precious is not found everywhere. So doing true חסד the right way is a rare chance, not something anyone can just jump into.

phrases.english: the verse states:
“How precious is Your kindness, O God
(the earth is full of the kindness of the Lord), etc.”
phrases.notes: תהלים לו:ח. Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. The פסוק being quoted here is just 'how precious is Your kindness, God'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possible mistake raised in step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone can easily jump in and do חסד.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing חסד properly is precious and rare.

steps.title: Is it rare even for a God-fearing person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe even a ירא שמים rarely gets the chance to do חסד properly?
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even a ירא שמים is like this, and also rarely gets the chance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a follow-up 'you might think.' This sets up the final פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 taught that proper חסד is rare. The גמרא now asks whether this applies to everyone, even a ירא שמים.

phrases.english: One might have thought that even a God-fearing person is the same —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the rule from step 28 applies to everyone.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the rarity of proper חסד reaches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If proper חסד is rare, maybe even a ירא שמים does not get the chance.

steps.title: The God-fearing are given the chance to do kindness
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק‎ 'ה׳'s kindness is forever upon those who fear Him' shows that a ירא שמים is given the chance to do חסד properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'And ה׳'s kindness is from forever to forever upon those who fear Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 29 with a פסוק and closes the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For most people, proper חסד is rare. But the פסוק says ה׳'s חסד is always upon those who fear Him. So a ירא שמים is helped from Above to find real chances to do חסד.
steps.whatToRemember: Doing חסד properly is a rare and precious chance, but a ירא שמים is given that chance by ה׳.

phrases.english: the verse states:
“But the kindness of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting
upon them that fear Him.”

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְחֶסֶד ה׳ מֵעוֹלָם וְעַד עוֹלָם עַל יְרֵאָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 29 and closes the section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even a ירא שמים rarely gets to do proper חסד.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ירא שמים is always given the chance to do חסד.

steps.title: A person with grace is surely God-fearing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר פפא teaches that anyone who has חן is certainly a ירא שמים. He brings the same פסוק used just before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר פפא said: Any person who has grace about him, it is known that he is God-fearing. As it says: 'The kindness of ה׳ is forever upon those who fear Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a teaching that uses the same פסוק from the previous step. Here the פסוק is read in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said: if you are a ירא שמים‎, ה׳ gives you חסד. רבי חמא בר פפא turns it around: if you see that a person has חן (grace, kindness that people feel), that is a sign he is a ירא שמים. The חסד resting on him is the signal of his fear of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Grace; a pleasant quality that makes people like someone
It is certain / it is known

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama bar Pappa said:
Any person who has grace upon him,
it is certain that he is God-fearing,
as it is said: 'The kindness of ה׳ is from everlasting'
'to everlasting upon those who fear Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק as step 30, but reads it in reverse: from a sign (חן) back to its cause (יראת שמים).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who has חן is certainly a ירא שמים, because ה׳'s חסד rests on those who fear Him.

steps.title: What is a Torah of kindness?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes the פסוק 'ותורת חסד על לשונה' and asks: is there a Torah that is not of חסד?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: What does the פסוק mean, 'She opens her mouth with wisdom, and a Torah of kindness is on her tongue'? Is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah that is not of kindness?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק from משלי and asks a question about its wording. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'Torah of kindness' implies there is also a kind of Torah that is not kindness. That seems strange, because all Torah is good. So we need to understand what difference the פסוק is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
She opens her mouth with wisdom (משלי לא:כו)
But is it so that...? (introduces a puzzled question)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: What is that which is written:
'She opens her mouth with wisdom,'
'and a Torah of kindness is on her tongue'?
Is there, then, a Torah of kindness
and a Torah that is not of kindness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching by רבי אלעזר on the חסד theme, now applied to Torah learning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of Torah is 'of kindness', and what kind is not?

steps.title: Torah learned for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: Torah learned לשמה is תורה של חסד. Torah learned שלא לשמה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: Torah learned for its own sake is a Torah of kindness. Torah learned not for its own sake is a Torah that is not of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers רבי אלעזר's question with the first explanation. The difference is the learner's motive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah itself is the same either way. What changes is why the person learns it. Learning with a pure heart, for the sake of the Torah, makes it 'kindness'. Learning for honor or other gain does not earn that title.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own sake; with a pure motive
Not for its own sake; for another motive

phrases.english: Rather: Torah studied for its own sake —
that is a Torah of kindness;
not for its own sake —

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא תּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל חֶסֶד.
phrases.english: that is a Torah that is not of kindness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is the motive: Torah לשמה is 'of kindness'; Torah שלא לשמה is not.

steps.title: Second version: Torah learned in order to teach
steps.stepSummary: Some say the difference is whether the person learns in order to teach others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Torah learned in order to teach it is a Torah of kindness. Torah learned without intending to teach it is a Torah that is not of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, 'kindness' means sharing. Learning so that you can pass Torah on to others is an act of חסד toward them. Keeping your learning to yourself is not called 'Torah of kindness'.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to teach it to others

steps.whatToRemember: 'תורת חסד' is explained two ways: (1) Torah learned לשמה, or (2) Torah learned in order to teach others.

phrases.english: Some say: Torah studied in order to teach it —
that is a Torah of kindness;
not in order to teach it —

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא תּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל חֶסֶד.
phrases.english: that is a Torah that is not of kindness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative explanation of the same פסוק, in place of the explanation in step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Torah learned in order to teach others is 'of kindness'; Torah not learned for teaching is not.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: water drawing on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about how the water ceremony was done on שבת, to discuss it next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'As its performance during the week,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה is over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes the opening words so it can ask a question next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the water ceremony on שבת was the same as on a weekday, except that the water was not drawn on שבת. Instead, on ערב שבת they filled a golden barrel that was not consecrated and placed it in a chamber. The water for שבת came from that barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is done on a weekday
Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted words are short, but the גמרא's question is about the rest of the משנה: the golden barrel that was 'not consecrated'.

phrases.english: As its performance during the week, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת the water was drawn on ערב שבת and kept in an unconsecrated golden barrel.

steps.title: Why not use a consecrated barrel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה insists on an unconsecrated barrel instead of a consecrated one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let him bring the water in a consecrated barrel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's detail that the barrel was not consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems more fitting to keep water meant for the מזבח in a holy vessel. So why does the משנה stress that the barrel was not consecrated?

phrases.english: And why?
Let him bring it in a consecrated barrel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail of the משנה quoted in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that the golden barrel be unconsecrated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A consecrated vessel seems more suitable for water used in the עבודה, so there is no clear reason to avoid one.

steps.title: זעירי: the water would become holy and be ruined overnight
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that this תנא holds there is no fixed amount for the water, and that כלי שרת make their contents holy even without intent. So a consecrated barrel would make the water holy, and it would become פסול by staying overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: This תנא holds there is no fixed measure for the water, and that כלי שרת make their contents holy even without intent.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי answers the challenge with two rules that this תנא holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because there is no set amount of water for the ניסוך, all the water in the barrel counts as fit to be made holy. Because a כלי שרת makes its contents holy automatically, even without anyone intending it, the water would become holy as soon as it entered the barrel. Holy items that stay overnight become פסול (לינה), so the water would be ruined by שבת morning. An unconsecrated barrel avoids this.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no fixed amount for the water
Holy vessels used in the בית המקדש
Make their contents holy even without intent

steps.whatToRemember: An unconsecrated barrel was used so that the water would not become holy early and be disqualified by staying overnight.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'לינה' does not appear on this amud. זעירי's statement continues at the top of the next amud with 'ונפסלין בלינה': holy water left overnight becomes פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being holy too early can be a problem. Holiness brings strict rules, such as the ban on לינה.

phrases.english: Ze'iri said:
He holds that there is no fixed measure for the water,
phrases.notes: So any amount in the vessel is fit to become holy.

phrases.english: and Temple vessels consecrate their contents even without intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר זְעֵירִי: קָסָבַר אֵין שִׁיעוּר לַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the legal opinions of the משנה's תנא that make a consecrated barrel harmful.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A consecrated barrel would be better for water meant for the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: A consecrated barrel would make all the water holy right away, and it would be disqualified by staying overnight. So an unconsecrated barrel is required.
